title: Bimodule objects and their morphisms
statement:
Let $(\mathcal C,\otimes,\mathbf 1,\alpha,\lambda,\varrho)$ be a monoidal category, with $\alpha_{X,Y,Z}:(X\otimes Y)\otimes Z\to X\otimes(Y\otimes Z)$, and let $(A,\mu_A,\eta_A)$ and $(B,\mu_B,\eta_B)$ be monoid objects [det-def-sfb-ring-object-monoid]. An $A$-$B$-bimodule is an object $P$ with actions $a_P:A\otimes P\to P$ and $r_P:P\otimes B\to P$ satisfying
$$a_P\circ(\eta_A\otimes P)=\lambda_P,\qquad a_P\circ(\mu_A\otimes P)=a_P\circ(A\otimes a_P)\circ\alpha_{A,A,P},$$
$$r_P\circ(P\otimes\eta_B)=\varrho_P,\qquad r_P\circ(r_P\otimes B)=r_P\circ(P\otimes\mu_B)\circ\alpha_{P,B,B},$$
$$r_P\circ(a_P\otimes B)=a_P\circ(A\otimes r_P)\circ\alpha_{A,P,B}.$$
Here an object in a tensor product of morphisms denotes its identity morphism. A morphism of bimodules $f:P\to Q$ is a morphism in $\mathcal C$ satisfying
$$f\circ a_P=a_Q\circ(A\otimes f),\qquad f\circ r_P=r_Q\circ(f\otimes B).$$
These objects and morphisms form the category of $A$-$B$-bimodules, with identities and composition inherited from $\mathcal C$; two bimodule morphisms are equal if their underlying morphisms are equal.
